adjustment_reviews.issue: The green step of criterion 1 ran past two guessed in-flight caps (13:55 and 14:15 UTC), each moved about a minute after it passed.
adjustment_reviews.evidence: Metric: cap moves per green 2 on criterion 1 (a3a9719 cap 13:55, 7c80c75 moved to 14:15, 406354e moved to 14:30) against 0 on criterion 2 (one note, cap 15:15 UTC, never passed; green 18f3962 at 14:54:16 UTC, origin/main = 18f3962 about 14:56). Counter-metrics: red to green 21 min (44112b4 14:33:05Z to 18f3962 14:54:16Z) against 62; no wait held past a cap. The suite really ran 14:36:50 to 14:53:59 UTC (17.2 min, 332 tests, 1 skip), so the true cap start + 25 was 15:01:50. But the rule was not applied as written: the developer did not report its suite start until the end, so the facilitator wrote the note (18cb108, 14:44 UTC) from an estimate, 'full suite expected to start about 14:50', which was 13 min later than the real start, and set cap 15:15. The cap did not move only because it was wide (13 min later than start + 25 from the true start). Criterion 2 is also a smaller change than criterion 1 (15 lines of green code in one file), so 21 min against 62 is not all the adjustment.
adjustment_reviews.side_effects: Good: no cap moves, no silence after a cap, the wait stayed visible. Bad: the cap came from the facilitator's guess of a start time it could not see, so the rule's key input (the measured start) was not used and the zero is partly luck; a wide cap hides a stalled suite for longer.
adjustment_reviews.verdict: tune: keep cap = suite start + 25 min, but the start must be the seat's own timestamp taken when the suite is launched and reported in the in-flight line, not an estimate (this stand-down's adjustment).
